name: Aubergine
description: A warm-season vegetable thriving in Mauritius's tropical climate. Produces glossy purple fruits ideal for curries and grills.
tips: Maintain consistent watering to prevent blossom-end rot.
Provide support stakes as fruits develop and become heavy.
Pollinate manually in enclosed hydroponic setups.

name: Basil
description: A fast-growing aromatic herb that loves Mauritius's warm temperatures. Perfect for DWC or NFT systems.
tips: Pinch off flower buds regularly to extend the harvest period.
Keep air circulation high to prevent powdery mildew.
Harvest in the morning for maximum flavor.

name: Bitter Gourd
description: A climbing vine prized in Mauritian cuisine. Known locally as 'margose', it thrives in the island's warm, humid conditions.
tips: Install a trellis system — vines can reach 3 to 4 meters.
Hand-pollinate for reliable fruit set in enclosed systems.
Harvest when fruits are still green for best flavor.

name: Bok Choy
description: A quick-growing leafy green that tolerates Mauritius's cooler highland winters. Excellent in stir-fries and soups.
tips: Cooler temperatures (below 20°C) produce sweeter, crispier leaves.
Ensure consistent moisture — dry spells cause bolting.
Harvest outer leaves progressively for a continuous yield.

name: Capsicum
description: Bell peppers and hot peppers flourish in Mauritius's year-round warmth. Rich in vitamin C and ideal for the local cuisine.
tips: Reduce nitrogen at fruiting stage to avoid excessive leaf growth.
Pollinate manually by gently shaking the plant.
Support heavy fruit clusters to prevent stem breakage.

name: Carrot
description: Best grown in cooler highland areas of Mauritius. Requires deep growing media for optimal root development in hydroponic setups.
tips: Use a deep media bed (at least 30 cm) for root development.
Avoid high nitrogen — it causes forked, hairy roots.
Thin seedlings to 5 cm spacing for uniform root growth.

name: Coriander
description: An essential herb in Mauritian cuisine. Fast-growing in cool conditions, prone to bolting in summer heat.
tips: Sow fresh seeds every 3 weeks for a continuous harvest.
Shade cloth helps prevent bolting during hot Mauritian summers.
Harvest leaves before flower stalks appear for best flavor.

name: Cucumber
description: A high-yield vine vegetable well-suited to Mauritius's tropical humidity. Excellent for NFT and DWC hydroponic systems.
tips: Train vines vertically on a trellis to maximize space.
Maintain high humidity to prevent powdery mildew.
Harvest frequently — every 2 to 3 days — to encourage production.

name: Green Onion
description: Quick-growing spring onions commonly used in Mauritian cooking. Thrives in both highland and coastal hydroponic setups.
tips: Regrow from cut bases — place root ends in shallow water.
Harvest at 30 cm height for optimal tenderness.
Good companion plant; can be interplanted with other crops.

name: Kale
description: A nutritional powerhouse that grows well in Mauritius's cooler highlands. Very productive in hydroponic NFT systems.
tips: Harvest outer leaves first to keep the plant producing.
Slight frost or cold stress sweetens the flavor naturally.
High calcium demand — watch for tip burn in fast-growing conditions.

name: Lettuce
description: The ideal starter crop for hydroponic systems in Mauritius. Fast-growing, low-maintenance, and thrives in DWC and NFT setups.
tips: Keep water temperature below 22°C to prevent tip burn.
Use shade cloth during Mauritius's hot summer months.
Harvest heads at 60 to 70 days, or outer leaves progressively.

name: Mint
description: Spearmint and peppermint grow vigorously in Mauritius. A kitchen staple used in drinks, desserts, and chutneys.
tips: Prune regularly — mint spreads aggressively and can crowd other plants.
Harvest just before flowering for peak oil content.
Propagate easily from cuttings placed directly in water.

name: Okra
description: Known locally as 'lalo', okra is a staple in Mauritian cooking. It loves heat and does exceptionally well in the island's climate.
tips: Harvest pods when they reach 7 to 10 cm for best tenderness.
Wear gloves — stems and leaves can be irritating to skin.
High heat tolerance makes it ideal for coastal lowland setups.

name: Pak Choi
description: A mild, crunchy leafy green popular in Chinese-Mauritian households. Grows rapidly in NFT channels and DWC systems.
tips: Ideal for beginners — tolerates a wide range of conditions.
Successive planting every 2 weeks ensures a continuous harvest.
High moisture needs — never let the roots dry out.

name: Pumpkin
description: A sprawling vine crop known locally as 'giraumon'. Needs space and strong support but rewards with abundant harvests.
tips: Hand-pollinate female flowers (with a round base) for fruit set.
Limit to 2 to 3 fruits per vine for larger, quality pumpkins.
Use a net sling to support heavy fruits as they mature.

name: Radish
description: One of the fastest crops to grow hydroponically. Perfect for beginners and short growing cycles in Mauritius.
tips: Harvest at 25 days — delay causes woodiness and bitterness.
Use a deep media bed for round varieties to form properly.
Thin to one seedling per pod for uniform root development.

name: Spinach
description: A nutrient-dense leafy green best grown in the cooler Mauritian highlands. Rich in iron and very popular in local cuisine.
tips: Avoid temperatures above 25°C — spinach bolts rapidly in heat.
Iron deficiency shows as yellowing between leaf veins.
Harvest baby leaves at 25 to 30 days for a tender crop.

name: Tomato
description: The most popular hydroponic crop in Mauritius. Cherry and beefsteak varieties thrive in DWC, NFT, and Dutch Bucket systems.
tips: Prune suckers weekly to focus energy on fruiting trusses.
Shake or vibrate the plant to aid pollination in enclosed setups.
Raise EC to 4 to 5 during fruiting for more flavorful tomatoes.

name: Watercress
description: A semi-aquatic herb that flourishes in hydroponic systems. Known locally as 'cresson', it's used in soups and salads.
tips: Prefers flowing water — DWC and NFT systems work best.
Harvest shoots continuously to prevent woodiness.
Cool highland water sources of Mauritius are ideal for this crop.
